recipes.name: Vegetable stock (Chaeso-gukmul 채소국물)
ingredients: 1 pound Korean radish or daikon, peeled and cut crosswise 1/2-inch-thick slices
1 dae-pa (large green onion) or 4 to 6 green onions, cut into 2 inch long pieces
5 ounces green cabbage leaves (about 2 cups), sliced
instructions: Combine the mushrooms, kelp, radish, onion, daepa (or green onions), and cabbage leaves in a large pot. Add 4 quarts (16 cups) water
Cover and cook over medium high heat for 30 minutes. If it begins to boil over, then open it, stir, and then put the lid back on but leave it slightly cracked.
Turn down the heat to medium and boil for another 30 minutes, until the radish is translucent and the stock is fragrant.
Remove from the heat. Put a mesh strainer over a large bowl and strain. You will have 10 to 11 cups of clear and light brown stock.
Reserve the cooked radish, kelp, and mushrooms to reuse. (See the recipes below)
Let cool and use whenever a recipe calls for stock. You can store it in airtight containers and refrigerate it up to 1 week or freeze for up to 3 months.
cooked kelp (5 to 6 ounces: about 150 grams) from making stock, sliced thinly
2 tablespoons vegetable oil
1 small onion, sliced
1 garlic clove, minced
4 teaspoons soy sauce
1 tablespoon rice syrup (or sugar), optional
1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil, optional
1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds, ground, optional
Heat a skillet over medium high heat. When the skillet is hot, add the oil. Add the kelp and stir-fry with a wooden spoon for 2 to 3 minutes, until the kelp looks a little springy and shiny.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce and rice syrup (if used), stirring another 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in sesame oil (if used) and sprinkle with the sesame seeds (if used). Transfer it to a plate and serve as a side dish for rice.
1 pound sliced and cooked radish from stock making
1 cup all purpose flour
1 cup stock (anchovy kelp stock or vegetable stock)
1 teaspoon kosher salt
vegetable oil
1 tablespoon soy sauce
½ tablespoon white vinegar
1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
Combine soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame seeds in a small bowl. Mix it well and set aside.
Combine the flour, kosher salt, and the vegetable stock in a bowl. Mix well.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium high heat. Add about 2 tablespoons vegetable oil and swirl the skillet to coat it evenly.

Dip each piece of the radish into the batter by hand or with tongs, making sure to coat both sides generously, and put it on the skillet. Get as much batter on the radish as you can, and use up all the batter. Work in batches so you don’t overcrowd the skillet.
Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes. Turn them over with a spatula and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes until both sides are golden brown.
Flip over and cook for another minute and transfer to a plate. Serve with the dipping sauce.
